questions.question: Can exhaustive petabase-scale mining of public sequencing archives, using RdRP as the marker gene, uncover a large hidden RNA-virus diversity that is absent from curated viral reference databases?
By what order of magnitude does the number of RdRP-defined sequence OTUs recovered from public archives exceed the RNA viruses catalogued in existing curated reference databases?
How does the RdRP-defined sOTU diversity recovered here compare in scale to existing curated viral reference databases?
Which ecological niches contribute the most previously-unknown RdRP lineages in this archive-scale screen?
Do the recovered RdRP fragments form monophyletic clades distinct from known viral families?
